## Motivation

Add the initial device, communication, and operator support for Cambricon MLUs. This builds on the MLU CI infrastructure introduced in [#41005](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41005) and enables its single-device and two-device suites to exercise SGLang runtime code.

Cambricon devices use the `mlu` device type provided by `torch_mlu` and CNCL for device communication. This PR adds an in-tree platform identity, integrates the communicator with SGLang's distributed layer, and adds an RMSNorm implementation backed by `torch_mlu_ops`.

The scope is limited to these foundations and their installation and tests. **This PR also provides tests to validate that the MLU CI infrastructure works end to end.**

## Modifications

### 1. Device platform and detection

- Add `PlatformEnum.MLU`, `DeviceMixin.is_mlu()`, and the in-tree `MluSRTPlatform`.
- Discover the MLU platform when no external platform plugin activates.
- Add device selection, memory queries, synchronization, cache management, and random-seed support.
- Detect MLU availability through `torch.mlu.is_available()`; an unavailable device returns `False`.

### 2. Distributed communication

- Add `MluCommunicator` and the `mlu → cncl` backend mapping.
- Route `GroupCoordinator.all_reduce()` and `all_gather()` through the MLU communicator.
- Disable the default PyNCCL path for MLU model-parallel groups and reuse the shared all-gather compatibility interface.

### 3. RMSNorm

- Add `forward_mlu` selection to `BaseFusedOp`.
- Implement RMSNorm and residual fusion using `torch_mlu_ops.fused_rms_norm`.

### 4. Installation and documentation

- Add `srt_mlu`, `all_mlu`, and `dev_mlu` extras to the shared `python/pyproject_other.toml`.
- Record the reference container tag and vendor component versions in `scripts/ci/mlu/component_versions.properties`.
- Document container creation, vendor package preparation, source installation, and CI suite verification. Vendor packages are obtained separately through Cambricon support.

### 5. Tests and CI integration

- Register `HWBackend.MLU`, `register_mlu_ci()`, and `--hw mlu`.
- Add `pr-test-1-mlu` for RMSNorm correctness and `pr-test-2-mlu` for two-device communication.
- Test RMSNorm against its native reference, including residual fusion, empty inputs, and non-contiguous layouts.
- Test all-reduce and all-gather through `GroupCoordinator → MluCommunicator`.
- Extend the existing CPU platform and fused-op dispatch tests.
- Update CI coverage reporting, registration lint, and slash-command backend recognition.

## MLU CI triggering

This PR adds MLU options to the existing label commands and a dedicated command for rerunning MLU CI. MLU PR tests require both `run-ci` and `run-ci-mlu`.

| Command | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `/tag-run-ci-label mlu` | Add `run-ci` and `run-ci-mlu`. |
| `/tag-and-rerun-ci mlu` | Add both labels, rerun unsuccessful CI workflows, and rerun the current commit's MLU workflow. |
| `/run-mlu-ci` | Add both labels and rerun only MLU CI. |

The updated labels are picked up on the next push or rerun. The label commands also accept `extra mlu` to opt into both tiers. Authorization reuses the existing permissions in `.github/CI_PERMISSIONS.json`.

The MLU suites cover:

- `pr-test-1-mlu`: single-device RMSNorm correctness.
- `pr-test-2-mlu`: two-device all-reduce and all-gather through the SGLang communicator.

## Accuracy Tests

Validated locally on Cambricon MLU hardware:

- RMSNorm numerical correctness against `forward_native()`, including residual and post-residual addition.
- Empty and non-contiguous RMSNorm inputs.
- Two-device all-reduce and all-gather through the SGLang communicator.

CPU tests cover platform interfaces and fused-op dispatch, including MLU forward selection and native fallback. Additional local checks verified non-default RMSNorm configurations against the native reference.

These are operator and communication checks. Model-level accuracy evaluation will accompany subsequent inference support.

MLU CI passed
([run](https://github.com/sglang-mlu/sglang/actions/runs/39231498205/attempts/5)):

- `pr-test-1-mlu`: 5 RMSNorm correctness tests passed.
- `pr-test-2-mlu`: two-device all-reduce and all-gather test passed.

This validates environment installation, hardware tests, and result/log reporting
through the MLU CI infrastructure.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No model-level throughput or latency benchmarks are included. This PR establishes the initial platform and CI coverage; inference benchmarks and profiling will accompany subsequent inference support.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

+def _run_mlu_communicator_worker(rank: int, world_size: int, init_method: str):
+
+    from sglang.srt.distributed.parallel_state import init_model_parallel_group
+
+    torch.mlu.set_device(rank)
+    dist.init_process_group(
+        backend="cncl",
+        init_method=init_method,
+        timeout=timedelta(seconds=60),
+        rank=rank,
+        world_size=world_size,
+    )
+    comm = None
+    try:
+        comm = init_model_parallel_group(
+            group_ranks=[list(range(world_size))],
+            local_rank=rank,
+            backend="cncl",
+            use_custom_allreduce=False,
+            use_mscclpp=False,
+            use_torch_symm_mem_allreduce=False,
+        )
+        assert comm.mlu_communicator is not None
+        assert not comm.mlu_communicator.disabled
+
+        x = torch.full((2, 3), rank + 1, dtype=torch.float32, device="mlu")
+        reduced = comm.all_reduce(x.clone())
+        expected_sum = torch.full((2, 3), 3.0, dtype=torch.float32, device="mlu")
+        torch.testing.assert_close(reduced.cpu(), expected_sum.cpu())
+
+        gathered = comm.all_gather(x, dim=-1)
+        expected_gather = torch.tensor(
+            [[1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2], [1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2]],
+            dtype=torch.float32,
+            device="mlu",
+        )
+        torch.testing.assert_close(gathered.cpu(), expected_gather.cpu())
+    finally:
+        if comm is not None:
+            comm.destroy()
+        dist.destroy_process_group()
+
+
+class TestMLUCommunicator(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_all_reduce_and_all_gather_on_cncl(self):
+        world_size = 2
+        self.assertGreaterEqual(torch.mlu.device_count(), world_size)
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
+            init_method = (Path(directory) / "rendezvous").as_uri()
+            mp.spawn(
+                _run_mlu_communicator_worker,
+                args=(world_size, init_method),
+                nprocs=world_size,
+                join=True,
+            )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

+
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+import torch_mlu  # noqa: F401 -- registers the MLU device backend
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_mlu_ci

+

+
+
+class TestRMSNormMLU(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.assertTrue(
+            torch.mlu.is_available(), "MLU device is required for this suite"
+        )
+        torch.manual_seed(42)
+        torch.mlu.set_device(0)
+        from sglang.srt.layers.layernorm import RMSNorm
+
+        self.norm = RMSNorm(128, eps=1e-6).to(device="mlu", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        with torch.no_grad():
+            self.norm.weight.normal_(mean=1.0, std=0.1)
+
+    def test_2d_input(self):
+        x = torch.randn(4, 128, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="mlu")
+        out = self.norm.forward_mlu(x.clone())
+        ref = self.norm.forward_native(x.clone())
+        self.assertEqual(out.shape, x.shape)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(out, ref, rtol=1e-2, atol=1e-2)
+
+    def test_residual(self):
+        x = torch.randn(4, 128, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="mlu")
+        residual = torch.randn_like(x)
+        out, residual_out = self.norm.forward_mlu(x.clone(), residual.clone())
+        ref, residual_ref = self.norm.forward_native(x.clone(), residual.clone())
+        torch.testing.assert_close(out, ref, rtol=1e-2, atol=1e-2)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(residual_out, residual_ref, rtol=1e-2, atol=1e-2)
+
+    def test_post_residual_addition(self):
+        x = torch.randn(4, 128, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="mlu")
+        residual = torch.randn_like(x)
+        post = torch.randn_like(x)
+        out, residual_out = self.norm.forward_mlu(
+            x.clone(), residual.clone(), post.clone()
+        )
+        ref, residual_ref = self.norm.forward_native(
+            x.clone(), residual.clone(), post.clone()
+        )
+        torch.testing.assert_close(out, ref, rtol=1e-2, atol=1e-2)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(residual_out, residual_ref, rtol=1e-2, atol=1e-2)
+
+    def test_empty_input(self):
+        x = torch.empty(0, 128, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="mlu")
+        self.assertEqual(self.norm.forward_mlu(x).shape, x.shape)
+        for post in (None, x.clone()):
+            out, residual = self.norm.forward_mlu(x, x.clone(), post)
+            self.assertEqual(out.shape, x.shape)
+            self.assertEqual(residual.shape, x.shape)
+
+    def test_noncontiguous_input(self):
+        x = torch.randn(128, 4, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="mlu").T
+        residual = torch.randn(128, 4, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="mlu").T
+        self.assertFalse(x.is_contiguous())
+        row_strided = torch.randn(8, 128, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="mlu")[::2]
+        for inp in (x, x.contiguous(), row_strided):
+            for res in (None, residual, row_strided):
+                with self.subTest(
+                    input_stride=inp.stride(),
+                    residual_stride=res.stride() if res is not None else None,
+                ):
+                    out = self.norm.forward_mlu(inp, res)
+                    ref = self.norm.forward_native(inp, res)
+                    if res is None:
+                        torch.testing.assert_close(out, ref, rtol=1e-2, atol=1e-2)
+                    else:
+                        for actual, expected in zip(out, ref):
+                            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                                actual, expected, rtol=1e-2, atol=1e-2
+                            )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
